newsitem.title: JAPAN: Nippon Express rejects air cargo rate hike request.
newsitem.headline: Nippon Express rejects air cargo rate hike request.

text.p: Nippon Express Co Ltd said on Wednesday that it had rejected requests by three European carriers for an increase in cargo rates.

A spokesman for Nippon Express, which is the largest transport company in Japan, said Air France, Lufthansa and KLM Royal Dutch Airlines NV had requested rate increases, but the forwarder had rejected them.
The three carriers want a 15 yen per kilogramme increase for cargo shipped from Tokyo, he said.
Japan's second-largest transport company, Kintetsu World Express Inc, also said it had rejected similar requests from the three.
Kintetsu World is a unit of Kinki Nippon Railway Co Ltd.
The carriers said the requests were due to increased fuel costs, the Japanese forwarders said.
The Nippon Express spokesman quoted the airlines as saying that the rate hike would only be temporary.
Both Japanese companies said they had rejected the requests because they were neither approved by the International Air Transport Association (IATA) nor Japan's Transport Ministry.
"Without approval by IATA and the ministry, it would be very difficult for forwarders to impose extra charges on their clients," the Nippon Express spokesman said.
